card.name: Hours in dosing interval phrases
card.fires_on: The time unit (hours, -hour, days) right after a number in dosing schedules like "every 4 hours" or "4 to 12 hours apart". Also fires on "of" in "at intervals of".

modes.label: Hours after a number
modes.description: The unit of time that closes a spacing phrase such as every N hours or N hours apart.
modes.example: Instill one drop in the affected eye(s) 3 times a day, 4 to 12<< hours>> apart for 7 days.

modes.label: Hyphenated hour before intervals
modes.description: The -hour piece in a phrase like 4-hour intervals.
modes.example: The recommended dosage of glycopyrrolate injection is 0.1 mg administered at 4<<-hour>> intervals, 3 or 4 times

modes.label: Interval wording
modes.description: Linking word or unit inside an "at intervals of" phrase.
modes.example: intrathecal methotrexate may be given at intervals of 2 to 5<< days>>.

card.writes: It promotes words meaning interval, spacing and frequency, which suggests the text continues by describing how far apart doses are.
card.plain: It lights up on the time unit in phrases saying how many hours apart doses are given.
